title: Micron reaches deal with Taiwan union to introduce quarterly profit bonuses in FY27
content: Micron Technology's labor dispute in Taiwan appears set for resolution after its Taichung union signed a labor-management agreement with the company and withdrew from the mediation session scheduled for October 22. According to an internal email circulated by employees, Micron will introduce quarterly profit-sharing bonuses based on employee level in fiscal year 2027. The plan will cover employees at the director level and below.

title: Li Auto chip subsidiary Mahe Xin raises CNY1.6 billion in equity financing as automakers aim to become chipmakers
content: Li Auto's chip and domain controller subsidiary, Mahe Xin Technology, has entered a first-round equity financing agreement worth CNY 1.625 billion (approx. US$243.33 million). The fundraising follows the automaker's recent opening of its in-house technologies to external customers, mirroring similar moves by other Chinese EV companies.

title: Cloud AI to drive chip growth in 2027 as Taiwan suppliers seek opportunities beyond weak consumer edge AI
content: Market expectations for cloud AI demand have generally remained bullish through 2028-2029, with order visibility extending clearly over the next two to three years. The outlook for 2027 is therefore similarly positive.

title: Infineon, Wolfspeed pivot to 8-inch SiC to cut costs and meet rising AI power demand
content: Infineon Technologies and US-based silicon carbide (SiC) leader Wolfspeed announced on October 15 a new multi-year supply agreement for 8-inch SiC wafers. This deal transitions their existing supply partnership from 6-inch to 8-inch substrate technology, positioning both companies to meet future demand across electric vehicles (EVs), renewable energy systems, and AI data center power infrastructure.

title: Sony keeps chip unit as imaging sensors, TSMC partnership drive strategy
content: Sony Group will not spin off its semiconductor business, which focuses on image sensors, president and CEO Hiroki Totoki said recently. The group is retaining the unit because its imaging-sensor expertise creates synergies between components and creative production, while a partnership with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) will support future manufacturing investment.

title: Samsung shifts M2800 modem to 2nm, frees 4nm capacity for HBM base dies
content: Samsung Electronics is transitioning its 4nm production capacity to HBM, with its next-generation mobile modem, the M2800, set to move to a 2nm process. The freed 4nm capacity will primarily support production of HBM base dies, which handle control functions at the bottom of HBM stacks.

title: HD Hyundai Robotics unveils dual-arm robot as FIX 2026 opens
content: HD Hyundai Robotics unveiled a dual-arm robot under development at FIX 2026 in Daegu, South Korea, on October 21, marking its first public showing as the company seeks to expand beyond conventional industrial automation into humanoid systems designed for factory work.

title: Samsung, SK Hynix reportedly upgrading China NAND fabs to fend off YMTC amid softening US stance
content: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are upgrading their NAND flash factories in China to make chips with more than 200 layers, Reuters reported on October 21, citing four people familiar with the plans. The move would let the South Korean memory makers win back ground lost to Yangtze Memory Technologies Co (YMTC), even though US curbs on upgrading their China operations remain formally in place.

title: Micron's Taichung union deal eases Taiwan DRAM strike risk; Taoyuan dispute remains unresolved
content: With a strike by Micron Taiwan employees looming, Micron Technology said Micron Memory Taiwan and the Taichung chapter of the Taiwan Micron Memory Union had reached agreement on several issues after multiple rounds of constructive discussions. The two sides signed a labour-management agreement and agreed to withdraw the mediation scheduled for October 22. Micron will continue talks with its Taoyuan union, which has planned a one-day strike for that date.

title: Anthropic's IPO spotlight falls on its potential US$750 billion AI compute tab
content: Anthropic's draft IPO prospectus captures the tension behind its rapid growth: first-half revenue surged to US$16.3 billion, while the company reported a US$80.7 billion net loss and outlined potential computing commitments of up to US$750 billion.

title: Murata develops world's smallest NTC thermistor, targets 2027 mass production
content: Japan's Murata Manufacturing has developed the world's smallest NTC thermistor, the 008004 NCU01 series, measuring 0.25mm × 0.125mm. Compared with Murata's previous smallest 01005-inch thermistor, measuring 0.4mm × 0.2mm, the new product cuts mounting area by about 60% while maintaining equivalent temperature-sensing performance, with both resistance and B-constant tolerances at ±1%.

title: China launches state-owned data group as market-facing arm of its AI infrastructure push
content: China has established a new state-owned enterprise, National Data Group, headquartered in Xiong'an, Hebei province. Ding Xuexiang, a vice-premier of the State Council, attended its inauguration on October 20.

title: PCB material shortages persist as capacity expansion extends beyond 2029
content: Rapid advances in AI and high-performance computing (HPC) are driving printed circuit boards (PCBs) toward higher layer counts, greater density, and higher-performance materials, triggering an open-ended shortage of upstream materials and equipment. Key suppliers of copper-clad laminates (CCL), copper foil and drill bits are launching capacity expansion plans covering the next 3-4 years.

title: Qualcomm plans global performance-based layoffs from November
content: Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon told employees in a memo on October 19 that the company will conduct global, performance-based layoffs after completing its annual employee evaluations, with notifications expected to begin in November. The move aims to build a stronger performance culture and address the company's continued failure to meet expectations.

title: US sanctions five Chinese entities over trade secret theft tied to ex-Google engineer
content: The US imposed sanctions on five Chinese entities tied to ex-Google engineer Linwei Ding for theft of trade secrets. The action follows his conviction for stealing confidential AI technology from Google, apparently to benefit Chinese firms.
